sources_considered.why: Primary recall filing documents a specific collision hazard and the remedy.
A 2024 evaluation directly tests generalization to difficult driving scenarios.
Contemporaneous operator safety results provide material context against interpreting the claim as blanket failure.
The underlying NHTSA recall filing was accessible and preferred.

evidence_items.locator: Page 2, Description of the Safety Risk
evidence_items.explanation: Waymo's filing documents a utility-pole collision under a particular combination of mapping and perception conditions. It also records a software and map remedy, showing that this specific defect was addressed.

evidence_items.locator: Section IV-A, Generalization of state-of-the-art Planning Methods
evidence_items.explanation: The interPlan study tests difficult scenarios and finds failures among both learned and rule-based planners. Its improved hybrid planner is evidence of progress, but the study does not demonstrate a broadly solved generalization problem.

evidence_items.locator: Section How the Waymo Driver Reduces Crash Rates
evidence_items.explanation: Waymo reports fewer injury and airbag-deployment crashes than its human benchmarks over more than 22 million driverless miles. These aggregate results show substantial practical success, but do not directly measure generalization to unfamiliar edge cases.

unresolved_gaps: The technical evaluation does not cover every proprietary driving system.
No finite set of incidents or benchmarks proves the nonexistence of every possible general solution.
